idea: A specialty coffee kiosk at a Barcelona metro exit, €3 flat whites for commuters

mia.title: Specialty coffee kiosk in Barcelona
mia.one_liner: Specialty coffee at the metro exit, open from 7:00.

brief.concept: A 12 m² takeaway-only specialty coffee kiosk at a busy Eixample metro exit, two-drink morning menu, €3 flat whites.
brief.for: Office commuters aged 25 to 45 who buy coffee on the way in and leave queues that take over 3 minutes.
brief.goal: Prove the pace with a pop-up cart selling 110+ cups a morning, and intent with 100 paid pre-orders, before any lease.

checklist.task: Count 7:00–9:00 footfall at two metro exits
checklist.how: Stand at each exit on Tuesday and Thursday and tally everyone leaving, in 15-minute blocks.
checklist.done_when: Four 2-hour counts logged; busiest exit chosen

checklist.how: Ask where they bought it, what it cost and what annoyed them; never ask if they would buy.
checklist.done_when: 20 logged; 8+ bought coffee on the way in

checklist.task: Shortlist three kiosks or shopfronts under 15 m²
checklist.how: Walk 300 m around the chosen exit and call every listing for rent, licence and term.
checklist.done_when: Three options with rent, licence and earliest start

checklist.task: Run a two-morning pop-up cart at the exit
checklist.how: Rent a cart and machine for two days and sell flat whites at €3.00 from 7:00 to 9:30.
checklist.done_when: 110+ cups each morning; median wait under 2 minutes

checklist.task: Get two espresso machine lease quotes
checklist.how: Ask two local suppliers for a 24-month lease including service and grinder.
checklist.done_when: Two written quotes, both under €700 a month

checklist.task: Choose the name and print 200 cup sleeves
checklist.how: Pick one of Nova's three names after asking ten cart customers which they remember.

checklist.task: Send the pre-order page to every contact
checklist.how: Message all interviewees, cart customers and two neighbourhood groups with the €2.40 offer.

checklist.task: Post the pre-order launch on Instagram and email
checklist.how: Publish Rae's week-3 posts and reply to every comment within the hour.
Hand cards at the exit 7:30–9:00 for three mornings and follow up anyone who opened the page.

checklist.task: Decide: sign a lease or stop
checklist.how: Compare cart sales and pre-orders with Sam's break-even line and Leo's kill criteria.
checklist.done_when: Decision written down with the numbers

leo.headline: Own the 7–9 am gap before cafés open.
leo.summary: Commuters already pay about €3 for coffee, but most specialty cafés nearby open after 8:30. It works if one kiosk can serve a flat white in under two minutes.

signals.name: Demand
signals.why: Thousands leave a central exit every weekday morning

signals.name: Price acceptance
signals.why: Commuters already pay €2.50–€3.50 for worse coffee

signals.name: Channel
signals.why: The street sells; social reach is unproven

signals.name: Timing
signals.why: Office attendance steady midweek, weaker Mondays and Fridays

leo.why_go: The demand walks past the door every morning, the price is already accepted, and the best competitors are closed at the moment that matters.

risks.risk: Rent beside a metro exit can eat the margin.
risks.mitigation: Cap rent at €3,800; a 12 m² takeaway counter, no seating.

risks.risk: Queues over 3 minutes break the habit.
risks.mitigation: Two-drink menu; time 50 orders at the pop-up cart.

risks.risk: Most commuters have never paid in Bitcoin Cash.
risks.mitigation: QR on the cart and the sleeve; count reservations and payments separately.

leo.next_step: Run a two-morning pop-up cart at the busier exit: 110 cups a morning at €3.00 is the bar.

market_facts.fact: A central Eixample metro exit typically sees several thousand people leave between 7:00 and 9:00.
Specialty flat whites in central Barcelona usually cost €2.80 to €3.80.
Most nearby specialty cafés open between 8:00 and 9:00, after the commuter peak.
One barista on a two-group machine can serve roughly 60 drinks an hour.
Takeaway kiosks near busy exits usually rent for €2,500 to €4,500 a month.

competitors.name: Office coffee machine
competitors.note: Free, but nobody looks forward to it

interviews.who: Commuters leaving the busiest exit between 7:00 and 9:00
interviews.where: At the exit itself and in two nearby co-working lobbies
questions: Where did you get coffee yesterday morning, if anywhere?
How long did you wait for it?
When did you last skip coffee because of a queue?
interviews.good_sign: They name a place and a price instantly, and have skipped coffee because of a queue this month.

kill_criteria: Stop if fewer than 8 of 20 commuters bought coffee on the way in yesterday.
Stop if the cart sells under 95 cups a morning, half the break-even pace.
Stop if no kiosk near the exit rents for under €4,500 a month.
leo.verdict_rule: Go from 7.0 with no signal at 3 or below · Pivot 5.0–6.9 · No-go under 5.0

confidence.note: Desk estimates only, no web sources: signals capped at 7.5. Interviews decide.

memo.purpose: A takeaway specialty coffee kiosk at an Eixample metro exit, for commuters who want good coffee before 9:00.
memo.problem: Between 7:00 and 9:00 commuters choose between fast generic coffee and good coffee that opens too late. Long bakery queues make many skip it.
memo.insight: The best competitors are closed at the exact moment demand peaks. A fast two-drink menu can own that window without competing on seating or food.
memo.verdict_line: Go, to test: it needs 186 sales a day to break even, and the plan reaches 300 by month 12.
